title: Total domination in the regular 4-polytopes
statement: A set D of vertices is totally dominating when every vertex, in D or not, has a neighbour in D; the total domination number gamma_t is the smallest size of such a set. Determine gamma_t for the graphs of the six regular convex 4-polytopes (the 5-cell K5; the tesseract, 16 vertices; the 16-cell, 8 vertices; the 24-cell, 24 vertices, 8-regular; the 600-cell, 120 vertices, 12-regular; the 120-cell, 600 vertices, 4-regular) and of the two E8 polytopes 3_21 (Gosset, 56 vertices, 27-regular) and 4_21 (the 240 roots of E8, 56-regular), each vertex adjacent to its nearest neighbours. First values (ours): the 5-cell 2 (exact); the tesseract (8-cell) 4 (exact); the 16-cell 2 (exact); the 24-cell 4 (exact); the 600-cell 16; the 120-cell 194; the Gosset polytope 3_21 4 (exact); the E8 root polytope 4_21 9. The headline cell is the 120-cell: find a certificate with value 193 or less (gamma_t >= n/d for a d-regular graph: >= 150 for the 120-cell), or prove 194 optimal.
submission: Text file: the vertex numbers of the set (spaces or newlines), in the checker's vertex order (the 120-cell).
score: the number of vertices in the set (smaller is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 10 November 2026: 194 for the 120-cell, best found: CP-SAT (one worker, 5 to 60 seconds) on the model of tools/polytope_sets.py, or, for zero forcing and power domination, greedy completion and pruning between rounds of fort cuts

context: Total domination (Cockayne, Dawes and Hedetniemi 1980) asks for monitors that are themselves monitored; for a d-regular graph gamma_t >= n/d, with equality exactly when the graph has a total perfect code (every vertex has exactly one neighbour in D): the bound is 10 for the 600-cell, 150 for the 120-cell, 3 for 3_21 and 5 for 4_21. Henning and Yeo's monograph collects the known values (paths, cycles, grids, some products and hypercubes); for these polytope graphs nothing was found.
references: E. J. Cockayne, R. M. Dawes, S. T. Hedetniemi, Total domination in graphs, Networks 10 (1980) 211-219
M. A. Henning, A. Yeo, Total Domination in Graphs (Springer 2013)
H. S. M. Coxeter, Regular Polytopes (3rd ed., Dover 1973)
the vertex numbering of checkers/orig_phys.py (polytope_graph), shared by every polytope problem of the Originals

novelty.verdict: new. No total domination result for the 600-cell, the 120-cell, the 24-cell or the E8 polytopes (searched with E8 and Gosset) was found on arXiv, in the journal literature (Crossref) or by web search; the known values for hypercubes and complete graphs cover only the small cells.
closest: General results on total domination (the references) and its values for hypercubes, grids and products; none for these polytopes.
Our polytope problems (polytope-ising, potts3-600, cell600-idcode, cell600-forest, cell120-coil, e8-idcode, e8-resolving): other invariants of the same graphs.

All cells: the 5-cell 2 (exact); the tesseract (8-cell) 4 (exact); the 16-cell 2 (exact); the 24-cell 4 (exact); the 600-cell 16; the 120-cell 194; the Gosset polytope 3_21 4 (exact); the E8 root polytope 4_21 9. Bound: 150 (gamma_t >= n/d for a d-regular graph, for the 120-cell).
